=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15797-15804 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: For stop markers other than project-failed, the state check verifies only that the stop label is present on the tracking issue and that PROJECT_STATUS is not in_progress or complete. It does not verify that PROJECT_STATUS matches the actual blocked state the verdict was issued for.
  WHY: A project like security-pass that was previously stuck at security-pass-failed and still carries the stale ai:security-pass-failed label (or an attacker re-adds it alongside ai:unblock-closed) passes the check because the stop label exists, the state is not in_progress or complete, and the code accepts it as authorized. The project is abandoned and its tracking issue closed despite not being in the blocked state the verdict addressed. The test at test_unblock_scan.py:276-278 treats security-pass as an authorized close, confirming the defect.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15788-15789 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The state_after jq regex tests whether a comment body matches ^<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 --> on a single line, but the actual V1 state-comment format uses a two-line delimiter: the opener is <!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 (no closing --> on that line) and the closer is ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 --> on a separate line. The regex never matches a genuine V1 state comment.
  WHY: A legacy V1 state write after a close verdict is invisible to state_after, so a close marker issued before the V1 write would still be accepted, even though a later state update exists. In practice this is low risk because post_state_comment only writes V2 chunks and legacy V1 comments predate close verdicts, but the code does not match what it declares.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: line 15802 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex check for newer orchestrator state markers in `state_after` does not correctly match V1 state markers.
  WHY: The regex `^<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` expects the V1 marker to end with ` -->` on the opener line, but the V1 format uses a separate closer line (`ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->`). A newer V1 state write will not be detected, allowing an earlier close verdict marker to be accepted even if a newer V1 state write exists.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | Code reference: the jq regex added in the last run, used by the new `state_after` check inside `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks` (the original PR introduces the function around line 15764; the LAST RUN DIFF wraps the existing verdict-extraction pipeline with `. as $comments | . as $verdict | . + {state_after: any($comments[]; ... test("^<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V(1 -->|2 part=[0-9]+/[0-9]+ manifest=[0-9a-f]{64} -->)"))}`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The V1 alternation branch expects the V1 state opener `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` on a single line, but the real V1 state comment format is multi-line: the opener is the bare `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` line, the JSON payload sits between, and the closer `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` is on its own line.
  WHY: The V1 branch is dead code today, so `state_after` only ever sees V2 state comments — which is fine because every state write after this PR is V2 (`post_state_comment` at line 2371 only writes V2 chunks). The bug does not change the new test `test_project_close_refuses_a_verdict_before_a_later_failure_state` because the test feeds a single-line fake `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` comment that the regex happens to match. If a real V1 comment ever gets posted after a new close verdict (e.g. legacy tracking issues reactivated by a backfill), the state_after branch will silently miss it and the close will proceed even though a newer state write exists.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 15789; V1 state-comment format at 2821 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `state_after` matcher requires the V1 opener to end with ` -->`, but the supported V1 format opens with `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` and closes on a separate line.
  WHY: During an engine rollout, an already-running older poller can write a V1 state comment after a trusted `close` verdict. The hook misses that newer state write; if the project is subsequently failed again with the same stop label, the stale verdict can still authorize abandoning and closing the tracking issue.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 15789 (the `state_after` jq regex) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The V1 alternation branch expects `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` on the opener line, but the actual V1 state-comment format uses `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` as the opener (no `-->`) with `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` as a separate closer line.
  WHY: The `state_after` check would not detect a later V1 state comment, allowing an earlier close marker to be accepted even when a newer pipeline-authored V1 state write exists. The test `test_project_close_refuses_a_verdict_before_a_later_failure_state` uses the incorrect single-line V1 format `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->`, so it passes but does not cover the real V1 format. Mitigating factor: `post_state_comment` only writes V2 chunks in current code, and legacy V1 comments predate new close verdicts, so this is unlikely to trigger in practice.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 15797-15803 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For stop markers other than `project-failed`, the state check rejects only `in_progress` and `complete` statuses, accepting `security-pass` and `security-pass-fixing` states when the matching stop label is present.
  WHY: If a project is in `security-pass-fixing` state (active fix cycle) but still carries the `ai:security-pass-failed` label from a prior terminal state, and an unblock judge close verdict with `stop=security-pass-failed` exists, the hook would honor the close even though the project was revived. The `state_after` check would only catch this if a newer state write has a higher comment ID than the verdict. The test `test_project_close_requires_current_trusted_verdict_and_retries_failed_close` treats `security-pass` status with `stop=security-pass-failed` as authorized, confirming this behavior is intentional but potentially unsafe if security-pass state can transition from terminal back to active without label removal.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | Code reference: handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks, state_after jq regex — `test("^<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V(1 -->|2 part=[0-9]+/[0-9]+ manifest=[0-9a-f]{64} -->)")` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The V1 alternation branch expects `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` on a single line, but the actual V1 state comment format (confirmed at line 2821: `sed -n '/^<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1$/,/^ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->$/p'`) uses `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` as the opener with no ` -->` suffix, and `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` as a separate closer line. The V1 regex branch will never match a real V1 state comment.
  WHY: In practice this is dead code — `post_state_comment` (line 2371) only writes V2 chunks, so no new V1 state comments are created after a close verdict. Legacy V1 comments predate any new verdict (lower comment IDs), so `state_after` (which looks for IDs > verdict ID) never needs to detect V1. The V2 branch matches correctly. No runtime impact, but the test `test_project_close_refuses_a_verdict_before_a_later_failure_state` parametrizes with `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 -->` (synthetic single-line format), passing because the regex matches the synthetic string, giving false confidence that V1 detection works for the real format.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
